text:
Carlos (ACME): hey @Raj, after our CI token rotation this morning the devs started hitting 403 on project creation in the console. error payload says "insufficient_scope". We rotated via our CI provider (client_credentials) not manually. Happened ~09:12 UTC. can you triage?
Raj (Support): sorry to hear that — can you DM the project id and the token id used by your CI? quick check: did your token get re-created under a different oauth client or service account? :thinking_face:
Carlos (ACME): pasted the ids in DM. logs show the call and the 403, here's the sanitized request/response from our side:
```
POST /v1/projects
Authorization: Bearer tok_ABC123_CI
Response 403 {
  "error": "insufficient_scope",
  "message": "missing scope: projects:write",
  "code": 403
}
```
We didn't change RBAC on the project side. The token rotation was automated by our CI on schedule.
Maya (SRE): looking at the auth logs — the token was indeed reissued but now has scopes [projects:read, org:metadata] instead of [projects:write, projects:read]. The CI provider is exchanging client credentials with a different OAuth client (client_id mismatch) so Redwood's token-minting service falls back to a reduced default scope. TL;DR: rotation created a read-only token.
Tess (Customer Success): Carlos — for a quick workaround you can: 1) re-issue a token explicitly requesting projects:write scope from your CI integration, or 2) add the CI's service principal to the project with a role that grants write (temporary). we'll keep you updated while infra investigates. :+1:
Raj (Support): thanks @Maya — can you confirm whether the console's token validation sidecar is rejecting on missing scope only, or also checking token audience? if it's scope-only we can temporarily map that CI client to a permissive fallback role while customer fixes rotation.
Maya (SRE): it's scope-first; audience matched. we see an idp-driven scope normalization rule that strips delegated scopes for certain client_types. i can reproduce locally:
```
# repro (local)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer tok_readonly_example" https://api.redwood.example/v1/projects -X POST -d '{"name":"tmp"}'
# response: 403 insufficient_scope
```
I'll open an internal ticket to update the idp-client mapping and also add clearer logging when a token is minted without projects:write.
ops-bot: deploy notification — rolled auth-logging patch to staging (build 2024.23.8) :robot_face:
Raj (Support): elevated to infra oncall and linked to the internal ticket. Carlos — if you can confirm the workaround (re-issue token) works we can close the support action; otherwise we'll push a temporary mapping and follow-up with a permanent fix.
Carlos (ACME): re-issued token requesting projects:write, verified project creation succeeded. thanks all. please keep me posted on the root cause so we can update our CI config.
Tess (Customer Success): noted — i'll send a postmortem template and best-practice steps for token rotation to Carlos after the internal ticket lands. :email:
Raj (Support): closing our support thread pending the internal fix, will reopen if anything regresses. thanks!
